summary: Client write-buffering causes out-of-order terminal events and interleaved partials on streaming responses
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (starting with NovaHealth) report streaming responses (SSE and WS) where final/terminal events arrive before some later partial tokens, or multiple 'end' markers appear interleaved with truncated choice fragments. Impact: Generated outputs are stitched incorrectly in the client UI, producing duplicated trailing phrases or missing punctuation. This affects user-visible completions and upstream validation logic. Environment: Production (us-east), NovaHealth dedicated pool behind their app-proxy. Observed with both SSE and websocket clients.

Observations: The pattern appears correlated with client libraries that implement their own write buffering on the POST/upgrade connection (e.g., buffering small writes into 64KB windows). When the client flush happens asynchronously the gateway sees a burst of bytes that contains multiple logical event fragments; our streaming proxy (nginx/keepalive settings + our buffering layer) sometimes reorders internal writes when handling concurrent keepalive probe responses, leading to out-of-order event boundaries delivered to downstream client, or duplicated trailing metadata frames. This differs from pure network disconnect/resume cases — there is no explicit reconnect recorded.

Needed: Investigate whether gateway buffering + streaming-proxy assembly is causing reassembly reordering and whether we should enforce per-connection sequencing and per-choice markers before forwarding. Also validate whether adding a small delimiter or enforcing chunked transfer boundaries on the gateway side mitigates the issue for apps that buffer writes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a long-running SSE generation call against /v1/stream with model redwood-8k-13b from a client that aggregates writes into 32–128KB windows (example: custom Java client using HttpUrlConnection with write buffering).
2) Client triggers token output frequently; client write flushes are coalesced into a single TCP burst on flush.
3) Gateway receives coalesced burst and forwards to streaming-proxy; streaming-proxy interleaves keepalive/probe responses during the same flush window.
4) Client reads SSE stream; final 'event: done' (or websocket 'DONE' control) appears before some preceding partial token fragments, or an extra terminal event is observed followed by more partials.

App logs: stitcher reported unexpected terminal then trailing tokens, caused validation failure on sentence boundary check.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): validated only observed from NovaHealth's custom client; reproduced partially with a synthetic client that buffers writes and flushes on timer (reproducer attached).

Hypothesis 1: multiple logical frames coalesced into one TCP write and our streaming-proxy delivery loop does not strictly preserve original logical ordering when interleaving keepalives or control frames — leads to sequencing gaps at the client parser.

Hypothesis 2: client-side parsing expects each SSE 'data:' chunk to be an atomic output; when multiple 'data:' entries are sent in a single write, some clients re-parse differently depending on newline boundaries.
Reproducer notes: a Go client that writes each SSE line individually shows correct behavior; Java client (HttpUrlConnection) default buffering replicates issue.
Metrics: small spike in 5xx errors is absent; no reconnection recorded in logs. No obvious CPU/GPU pressure on serving nodes.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported repeated cases in the last 48h; attached client HAR and custom Java client code. Asked NovaHealth to run non-buffered client for comparison.

Ethan Brooks (SRE) 2026-03-11: I reproduced locally with their client config. It looks like nginx sendfile + proxy buffering can reorder when keepalive is injected. Opening a side investigation on proxy code path. Linked PR suggestion: switch to 'tcp_nodelay' / flush-on-delimiters at gateway.

Sofia Martinez (Runtime) 2026-03-12: Suggest adding a streaming boundary marker (zero-length 'meta' event) on our side before forwarding terminal events to ensure clients pick correct finalization ordering. This will be low-risk feature flag behind gateway.
resolution: Workaround: Instruct customer to disable aggressive write coalescing in their client (flush more frequently) — NovaHealth validated this immediately and saw correct stitching. Temporary server-side mitigation: toggle gateway feature flag 'sse-enforce-chunk-boundaries' for NovaHealth dedicated pool to insert explicit newline separators between logical events. Long-term fix: implement strict per-connection sequencing in streaming-proxy and ensure keepalive/probe writes are serialized after logical event boundaries. Follow-up work: ENG-STREAM-612 to add unit tests and e2e reproducer suite. Rollout notes: feature-flag enabled for NovaHealth pool on 2026-03-12; monitoring for duplicates/timeline regressions for 72h.
regression_risk: Low-medium: change affects streaming proxy delivery ordering and may impact latency by an additional ~2-6ms per event when strict serialization is enabled. Feature flag guarded.
